paragraphs: Narada was a great sage among the gods, a fine yogi who travelled everywhere. One day, passing through a forest, he came upon a man who had been meditating so long that termites had built a mound around his body. The man asked where Narada was going. To heaven, Narada said. Then, the man asked, please find out from God when He will be merciful to me and set me free.

A little further on Narada met another man, leaping about, singing and dancing wildly. He too asked where Narada was headed, and when he heard 'heaven', he asked Narada to find out when he would be free.

Some time later Narada came back the same way. The man in the ant-hill eagerly asked what the Lord had said. Narada told him he would be free after four more births. The man burst into tears and wailed: he had meditated until an ant-hill grew around him, and still there were four more births to go!

Then Narada went to the dancing man. Do you see this tamarind tree? he said. You will be born as many times as there are leaves on it, and then you will be free. The man began to dance with joy at the thought that freedom would come so soon.

At that moment a voice spoke: my child, you shall have freedom right now. That was his reward for his perseverance. He was ready to go through all those births, and nothing could discourage him, while the first man found even four more births too long. Swamiji's point: only perseverance like this, willing to wait for ages, brings the highest result.
learn: Impatience can quietly undo years of effort. If you love the path itself, whether it is your studies, a skill or your inner growth, the time it takes stops feeling like a burden, and that cheerful persistence is often what gets you there.
